order.reason: Gives the four-step interview framework that frames how every later topic is used.
Covers RESTful API design tips such as idempotency, pagination and rate limiting that feed the high-level design step.
Introduces load balancers and how traffic is spread across servers, a core scaling building block.
Compares SQL and NoSQL so you can choose a database, which sharding and caching build on.
Teaches sharding methods and shard key choice for scaling the database tier horizontally.
Explains caching and its pitfalls like stampede and penetration, building on database knowledge.
Covers CAP theorem trade-offs, a distributed-systems concept best tackled after the scaling topics.

path_summary: Start with the interview framework, then API and load balancing basics, then databases, sharding and caching, and finish with CAP theorem trade-offs.

areas.why: A structured approach (scope, high-level design, deep dive, wrap-up) keeps the interview on track.
Estimating traffic, storage and bandwidth drives every sizing decision in a design.
Spreading traffic across servers is the first step to scaling and availability.
Picking the right data store and justifying the trade-offs is asked in almost every design.
Caching cuts latency and load, but stampedes and penetration must be handled.
Splitting data across nodes is how large systems scale writes and storage.
Distributed designs must reason about consistency versus availability under partitions.
Clean, scalable interfaces (naming, idempotency, pagination) are part of most designs.
Queues decouple services and absorb traffic spikes.
Protecting services from overload and failures is a common deep-dive topic.
Serving static and media content near users reduces latency and origin load.
